newsitem.title: KENYA: U.N. Rwanda trial HQ to get four more suspects.
newsitem.headline: U.N. Rwanda trial HQ to get four more suspects.

text.p: Four genocide suspects indicted by the U.N.'s Rwanda tribunal were being flown to the tribunal's headquarters from Cameroon late on Thursday, a spokesman said.
The four men include Theoneste Bagasora, the former cabinet director in Rwanda's defence ministry, accused of directing events in the first few days of the 1994 genocide.
"The four suspects from Cameroon will arrive by plane at 7 p.m. (1600 GMT) this evening," said tribunal spokesman Bocar Sy by telephone from Arusha.
"Nobody is allowed to go the airport by order of the Tanzanian authorities because of security," he said.
A total of 21 people have been indicted by the International Criminal Tribunal for Rwanda (ICTR) of whom seven are in custody at the tribunal's north Tanzania headquarters.
The tribunal was set up in November 1994 to bring to justice the architects of the Rwandan genocide in which an estimated 800,000 Tutsis and moderate Hutus were killed.
The trial of Jean-Paul Akayesu, a former mayor who has pleaded not guilty to genocide and crimes against humanity, started two weeks ago.
